chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'Subhan Allah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Anafa (transcendent dignity) for God.'

key_terms.أَنَفَةٌ: Anafa — transcendent dignity; noble disdain for what is unworthy; God's quality of being exalted above every deficiency
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Subhan Allah — the tasbih formula of glorification, affirming God's transcendence above all imperfection

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Subhan Allah' according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this brief but theologically dense hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ (Subhan Allah) as أَنَفَةٌ لِلَّهِ — God's inherent transcendent dignity, His quality of being too exalted to admit any imperfection or unworthy attribute. The term أَنَفَة in classical Arabic denotes noble pride and disdain for what falls beneath one's dignity; applied to God, it encapsulates His absolute tanzih (transcendence) over all deficiency, giving the act of tasbih a precise theological grounding.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about ‘Glorious is Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Respect of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following. “I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words Glorious is Allah.”
The Imam said, “It means Distinction of Allah (His being free of all shortcomings).”
